answer.generated: The two primary design issues in distributed systems engineering are transparency and openness. Transparency concerns how much the distributed system appears as a single system to users; it balances ease of use with the reality of multiple components. Openness addresses whether the system uses standardized protocols for interoperability or specialized protocols that limit flexibility. These issues are critical because they affect both usability and maintainability of the final product.
